transform.form: x = A + k*W*(cg - 88);   y = yAt1200 - pxPerLb*(W - 1200)
transform.why: The abscissa is not C.G. despite the caption: ray spacing grows with weight and the family pivots about C.G. 88, so x encodes moment about an 88-inch reference.

validation.note: Weight axis: last major tick is 2400 at y=581; the envelope top edge sits ~39 lb above it at 2440.

limitsAuthoritative.source: POH 2.13 Center of Gravity Limits (p2-4) and 2.11 Weight Limits (p2-3a)
limitsAuthoritative.note: 'Straight line variation between points given' - linear in C.G. vs weight. These govern.

printedCutout.extraction: 93 thick-stroke points, W 1955-2435, seeded search window; rms of the best fit 0.03-0.07 in
printedCutout.shape: Nearly straight in C.G.-vs-weight but with a real bow: a straight line in C.G. fits to rms 0.041 in (max 0.162), a straight line in the chart's own pixel space fits worse (0.066 in), and a quadratic best of all (0.031 in). So the drawn cutout is not straight on the chart - confirmed against a physical ruler on screen.
printedCutout.notCoincidentWithUtilityCeiling: the cutout begins at 1950 lb; the utility ceiling is a separate 2020 lb cap
printedCutout.vsTable: The drawing reaches C.G. 87.93 at max gross where 2.13 tabulates 88.3, i.e. the illustration is ~0.35 in MORE permissive at the top. The model therefore uses the 2.13 table, which is both the legal limit and the conservative one.
